fields.claim_quote:
Since the pair σ0 < σ1 is minimal among pairs of τ = σ0 ∪σ1, then writing τ = (t0, . . . , tk+1),
where i < j =⇒ti < tj, it follows that σ0 and σ1 must be of the form σ0 = {t0, . . . , tk−1} and
σ1 = {t0, . . . , tk−2, ˆtk−1, tk}. Therefore the common face of σ0 and σ1 is σ0 ∩σ1 = {t0, . . . , tk−2},
which is the minimal (k −1)-face of τ, as well as the minimal (k −1)-face of both σ0 and σ1.

fields.witness: Let k=2 and τ have ordered vertices t0=0<t1=1<t2=2<t3=3. Its 2-faces, represented by increasing vertex tuples, are 012<013<023<123. Thus the two lexicographically smallest are σ0={0,1,2} and σ1={0,1,3}; moreover σ0∪σ1=τ, and (σ0,σ1) is also the least ordered pair of distinct 2-faces whose union is τ.
